$comment: Known differences from the canonical implementation. `cases` are conformance cases whose resolutions this crate gets wrong; `rules` are lint rules it does not emit. This crate is a resolver, not a linter: it emits no diagnostic at all, so every rule is listed, each with what the crate does in the situation the rule reports. The runner in tests/corpus.rs fails when a ledgered case passes, when the ledger names a case the corpus does not have, and when the canonical implementation defines a rule that is not listed here, because a ledger that is not kept true stops being read.

cases.reason: A fragment of more than one step that starts at a block anchor, such as `#^limit/Sentence2`, is read as an invalid block id, so the reference is left out of the card's links and its resolution is missing.
cases.spec: HMD-0006, the address after the hash

cases.reason: A fragment of more than one step that starts at a block anchor, such as `#^limit/Sentence2`, is read as an invalid block id, so the reference is left out of the card's links and its resolution is missing.
cases.spec: HMD-0006, the address after the hash

rules.reason: A reference that resolves to no card. The outcome is `Resolution::Unresolved`; the warning is the caller's to report.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A bare reference that autodiscovery matches to more than one card. The outcome is `Resolution::Ambiguous` with its candidates; the error is the caller's to report.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A reference or an import that climbs above the namespace root. For a reference the outcome is `Resolution::Escapes`; an import that climbs out contributes nothing and is not reported.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A heading fragment the resolved card does not have. Headings and their slugs are not read, so a fragment is parsed and never checked.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A block fragment the resolved card does not have. Block anchors are not read, so a fragment is parsed and never checked.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A block identifier used twice in one card. Block anchors are not read.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: An embed cycle. Embeds are found and resolved, never expanded.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: An embed chain deeper than the bound. Embeds are found and resolved, never expanded.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: Frontmatter that is not valid YAML or not a mapping. Such frontmatter contributes nothing to resolution and is not reported.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A malformed or unterminated reference. A malformed reference is left out of a card's links; `Reference::parse` says why when a caller asks.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: Two headings in one card sharing a slug. Headings are not read.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A card beside a folder note of the same name. The card wins, as in the canonical implementation; the collision is not reported.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A malformed reserved frontmatter key. A malformed `use` entry is skipped; `tags` and `nav` are not read at all.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A malformed import statement. The statement is skipped and not reported.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: An import of a directory or a card that does not exist, or a local name bound twice. The import binds nothing, or the first binding stands, and neither is reported.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A reference that more than one imported directory holds. The earlier import wins, as in the canonical implementation; the later ones are not reported.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A published card that links to an unpublished one. The publication model is not read: `nav` is ignored and no card is public or private here.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do

rules.reason: A card shadowed by one of the same name with an earlier card extension. The earlier extension wins, as in the canonical implementation; `Vault::shadowed_by` names the winner, and the warning is the caller's to report.
rules.spec: HMD-0027, what the crate does not do; HMD-0029

rules.reason: A malformed address. This crate emits no diagnostic. Once addresses are resolved here, a failure is a typed error the caller reports; until then a fragment is parsed and never checked.
rules.spec: HMD-0006, the address after the hash

rules.reason: An address step that selects nothing in its scope. This crate emits no diagnostic. Once addresses are resolved here, a failure is a typed error the caller reports; until then a fragment is parsed and never checked.
rules.spec: HMD-0006, the address after the hash

rules.reason: A block step outside the section the address names before it. This crate emits no diagnostic. Once addresses are resolved here, a failure is a typed error the caller reports; until then a fragment is parsed and never checked.
rules.spec: HMD-0006, the address after the hash

rules.reason: A heading whose slug a short-form step reads as a count. This crate emits no diagnostic. Once addresses are resolved here, a failure is a typed error the caller reports; until then a fragment is parsed and never checked.
rules.spec: HMD-0006, the address after the hash

rules.reason: A quotation whose integrity digest no longer matches. This crate emits no diagnostic. Once addresses are resolved here, a failure is a typed error the caller reports; until then a fragment is parsed and never checked.
rules.spec: HMD-0006, the address after the hash
